implementation_notes: A Map whose values are factory functions is the entire pattern: register('circle', () => new Circle(1)), then create(name) resolves the key and calls it. MDN recommends Map over an object literal whenever keys are not known until run time, because Map keys may be of any type and a Map cannot inherit properties from Object.prototype, which matters the moment a key comes from user input. What replaces the classic structure: the map plus arrow functions; a module-scoped Map is naturally private to the kit, and nothing else is needed until the set of types must be closed, in which case a plain object plus a switch is smaller. Because module state is cached per process, the kit should expose a reset() or be created per test when the registry is genuinely mutable.
pitfalls: With a plain object as the table, keys such as constructor or toString hit Object.prototype; use a Map or Object.create(null) and never pass untrusted input straight into the lookup.
Duplicate registration silently overwrites when you rely on set() alone - check has() first if third parties may register.
Module state is shared by every importer and every test in the process, so a registration left behind by one test changes another; expose a reset or build the kit per suite.
